name: KIRIBATI

flag.title: Flag of Kiribati
flag.note: Frigatebird soars over a 17-rayed rising sun

lead: Kiribati (say "Kiribas") is 33 coral atolls (rings of coral islands) in the Pacific. They are so spread out that they touch all four hemispheres. Most land is barely 2 m above sea level. Today, I-Kiribati people fish, dance, and meet in open maneaba halls.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Kiribati's 33 atolls are scattered across the Pacific like confetti. They hold only 811 km² of land, less than Hong Kong. Storm waves are a constant threat.
Kiritimati (Christmas Island) holds nearly half the country's land. It is one of Earth's largest atolls. Only Banaba climbs to 87 m.
animals: The magnificent frigatebird rules Kiribati's skies and appears on its flag. Its wingspan reaches 2.3 m. The male puffs up a shiny red throat pouch to impress females.
The coconut crab is the world's largest land animal with no backbone. It weighs up to 4 kg, cracks coconuts with bare claws, and lives 60 years.
culture: Every village has a maneaba, an open-sided meeting house with a pandanus-leaf roof. Villagers meet there to debate, feast, and watch the te mwaie dance.
Dance styles copy the frigatebird's glide. There are eight styles, from slow seated buki to lively standing katei. Dance keeps old stories alive without a single written word.
history: Micronesian ancestors settled the Gilbert Islands over 2,000 years ago. Britain made them a protectorate in 1892. Britain then mined Banaba's phosphate and moved all the Banabans to Fiji.
In 1943, US Marines stormed Betio in Tarawa Atoll. 1,700 Americans died in 76 hours. Kiribati won independence from Britain on 12 July 1979.
wows: Kiribati is the only country in all four hemispheres.
Kiritimati is first to ring in every new year.
Two Kiribati islands vanished underwater in 1999, swallowed by rising seas.
The Phoenix Islands Protected Area is bigger than California.
More than half of Kiribati adults smoke, one of the highest rates on Earth.
Kiribati has no army, navy, or air force.
Fewer than 10,000 people live on Kiritimati, nearly half of Kiribati's land.

myths.myth: The date line is a straight line
myths.fact: It bends around Kiribati. In 1995 the country moved it east so every island shares one day.
Their feathers are not waterproof, so they never land on the sea. They can stay in the air for weeks.
